proof.text: Use the actual Godement mapping fibre K(A,I) and its augmentation. Choose the degreewise semilinear maps furnished by strict Godement functoriality. Its four equations give the first four clauses of the statement.
The Godement Cech comparison gives an augmented ordered localization model for each K(A,I), which is exactly the final clause of the statement.

For a K-flat resolution p:P to K(A,I), construct E as the actual termwise scalar extension functor and chi as the semilinear composite m after p, extended by adjunction. The pure-tensor normalization and differential formula are proved by the explicit lifting API. Transport the augmented Cech model backwards across p by composing its derived isomorphism with the inverse of Q(p). Apply the two-complex Cech base-change theorem, whose augmentation equation follows from functorial augmentation compatibility and the normalization. Thus chi is a quasi-isomorphism, so Q(chi) is invertible, as required.

title: Functorial ring complex for a finitely generated ideal
statement: For every commutative ring $A$ and finitely generated ideal $I\subset A$, there is a complex $K(A,I)$ of $A$-modules and an augmentation $K(A,I)\to A[0]$. Complexes and $D(A)$ use [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; modules use [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on the one-object site. For every ring map $\varphi:A\to B$ there is a $\varphi$-linear chain map $K(A,I)\to K(B,IB)$, compatible with compositions and augmentations. The induced map $K(A,I)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\to K(B,IB)$ is an isomorphism in $D(B)$; derived tensor is the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] after a K-flat replacement [def-pc-kflat-complex]. If $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$, allowing $r=0$, let $C_A(f)$ have degree-zero term $A$, degree-$q$ term $\prod_{i_1<\cdots<i_q}A[1/(f_{i_1}\cdots f_{i_q})]$ for $1\leq q\leq r$, and zero terms otherwise. Here $A[1/g]$ is localization at the powers of $g$; the differential is the alternating sum of localization maps, and the augmentation to $A[0]$ is identity in degree zero. There is an augmentation-compatible isomorphism $C_A(f)\cong K(A,I)$ in $D(A)$.
